learningObjective: Reason about a subtle event-timing bug where an event recorded on one stream is elapsed against an event recorded on another stream, giving a wall-time reading that is not the intended per-stream cost.

canonicalClaims.claim: Under legacy default-stream semantics, events recorded on the default stream synchronize with all other user streams; to isolate one stream's timing, both start and end events must be explicitly recorded on that stream.
conditions: Legacy default-stream mode (CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING or default per-context).
Multiple user streams with concurrent work exist.
nonImplications: Does not imply per-thread default stream mode has the same issue; that mode changes default-stream sync behavior.
Does not imply zero cross-stream interference; shared resources can still cause slowdown.

misconceptions.whyWrong: Events recorded on a specific stream do isolate that stream's progress.

misconceptions.claim: elapsed_time returns a union of concurrent activity; divide by stream count.
misconceptions.whyWrong: elapsed_time is the GPU wall time between two event completions; no divide semantics exists.
It only waits for the specific event to complete.

misconceptions.claim: Recording an event without specifying a stream is equivalent to recording on the target stream.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Without a stream argument the event is recorded on the default stream, which has special sync behavior.
